decisions.reason: The I2C series-resistor placement does not change the standalone USB supply, source selection, powered rail, or sensor-debugging power behavior.
The confirmed I2C signal topology does not alter DCDC1 voltage, current rating, regulation, or load coverage.
Placing series resistors between the ESP32-S3 pins and the pull-ups and devices does not change the sensor board's connector-fanout role or required ports.
The source decision changes I2C conditioning topology but does not change the interboard connector partition, connector types, signal pinout, or pin-order policy.
The I2C SDA/SCL series-resistor topology is independent of the MT3608 boost rail, GPIO5 enable control, and 5V sensor loads.
The decision confirms components placed after the ESP32-S3 I2C pins but does not reassign SCL0, SDA, SPI MOSI, or any other GPIO.
Referencing the ESP32-S3 pins in the conditioning topology does not change the selected controller family.
The I2C series-resistor placement does not affect the addressable LED supply, level shifting, data GPIO, or standby power control.
The source concerns I2C SDA/SCL conditioning and does not modify the charge-status LED interface or its series resistance.
The electrical ordering of I2C series resistors, pull-ups, and devices does not change the number or identity of the project's separate boards.
The referenced resistors are I2C signal-conditioning components, not the battery-protection resistors or protection circuitry.
The I2C signal topology does not change the AXP2101 battery input, normal-operation power source, or system-load coverage.
